correctness.rationale: Polarizing the fixed quartic in characteristic three gives W^(3)=W^perp on a line, so W^(9)=W; these two-spaces are precisely the totally isotropic Hermitian two-spaces over F9. Norm-fiber sizes 1,4,4 give 2241 isotropic vectors counting zero, hence 280 points; the binary Hermitian quotient above each point gives 4 lines, each with 10 points. The 48 pairing lines are distinct. The four nonproportional coordinate forms of the extra representative identify its projective monomial stabilizer with PGL2(F3) of order 24, so its disjoint orbit has size 1536/24=64. On either smooth quartic fiber adjunction gives N=O(-2), hence zero Hilbert tangents. The proper, quasi-finite line scheme is finite, and complete-DVR idempotent lifting followed by Nakayama makes each rational closed-point factor a quotient of R. Simple roots of T^4+1 lift the 48 pairing lines. Independently expanding the representative restriction gives mixed coefficient 2*binom(4,2)=12. Every chart lift modulo nine adds 3 times linear forms to the last two coordinates, and the cubes multiplying the first-order corrections reduce to u^3±v^3. Thus the mixed coefficient remains 3 modulo 9. Liftable coordinate symmetries transport this obstruction, so each extra factor is exactly R/(3). There are no Frobenius-fixed pairing lines. Over F3 there are eight totally isotropic lines of the split quadratic form: 16 isotropic projective points, two lines through each, and four points per line. Frobenius descent therefore gives the claimed 24 horizontal pairs, 8 rational vertical points, and 28 vertical pairs. The proof and exact coefficient replay establish the scheme, rather than just reproducing a finite point count.
residual_risks: The obstruction is for the fixed integral equation and embedded lines. Deforming the quartic itself or varying a characteristic-three pencil is not covered.
